gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Jackery sells an IP65-rated power station, the Explorer 1500 Ultra (1,536 Wh, $1,079 at Jackery US on 2026-11-13). ChatGPT's own answer only warned that most power stations are not waterproof and did not name one that is.
standout_why: The results ChatGPT got cover only the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (seven manual copies plus EcoFlow US pages for it and the older RIVER Plus), the BLUETTI AC70 store page and one GearRanking review of the RIVER 3 Plus. None of them covers a weather-rated unit, and none prices the 1 kWh class against itself. I could not open GearRanking (self-signed certificate error) or EcoFlow's RIVER 3 Plus page (HTTP 429), so I am judging those two from their titles and the URLs. That is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: If the station stays outside next to the lights, the Explorer 1500 Ultra is the only IP65 unit I found, and its $1,079 price is the cost of that rating. If the station sits under cover, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic is the value pick: $459 at EcoFlow US for 1,024 Wh, which is $20 less than the $479 Best Buy price ChatGPT showed and $40 less than the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2. For small string lights, the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ($289.99, 288 Wh) is the only small unit whose maker states a standby draw (4.5 W). That figure matters when the load is 10–30 W for hours.

findings.label: Price and standby draw
findings.value: $289.99; 288 Wh; 600 W AC; 4.5 W standby (maker's claim)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Portable Power Station | 600W 288Wh
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search. The listing says 'only 4.5W standby'. With a 20 W string light, 4.5 W of overhead is about 22% on top of the load. Loses on capacity: 288 Wh covers about 10 h of 20 W lights after overhead (288/(20+4.5) = 11.8 h before inverter losses), so it only suits small setups.
